clue.text: Heading west, curve around port

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west means the letters run right to left, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a curve is an arc
around is circa, abbreviated CA

explanation.surface: A ship heading west swings round a bend into harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading west' turns ARC + CA into the capital of Ghana.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital of Ghana and a seaport on the Gulf of Guinea.

clue.text: See 24
Portions from the chippy? Lunch boxes no longer have them!

definitions.meaning: a fish-and-chip shop (a British chippy) sells pieces of cod

definitions.text: Lunch boxes no longer have them!
definitions.meaning: lunch box is British slang for a man's genitals; the pouch covering them went out of fashion centuries ago

explanation.walkthrough: A chippy is a British fish-and-chip shop; 'lunch box' is jokey British slang for the male crotch.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudor pouch worn over the crotch of men's hose is no longer part of male dress.

clue.text: Pest starting off fast, hard to catch

indicators.note: to catch means the letter for hard is held inside the shortened word
starting off means the word for fast loses its opening letter

parts.note: fast means rapid
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A pest that is quick off the mark is hard to catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starting off' cuts RAPID to APID; 'to catch' puts H inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly and blackfly are sap-sucking insects that gardeners treat as pests.

clue.text: Moving in the right direction, having several training sessions?

definitions.meaning: a ship or a plan that is not straying from its route
someone attending a programme of classes is literally taking a course

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means heading correctly toward a goal, and also enrolled in a series of lessons.

clue.text: Exclusion of drunken sot with display of unacceptable bigotry

indicators.note: drunken describes the sot but also signals his letters reeling into a new order

parts.note: prejudice against other races is racism

explanation.surface: A drunk is shunned for spouting racist views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' rearranges SOT into OST, followed by RACISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostracism is social exclusion, being shunned by a group.

clue.text: Bird to sing, missing note

indicators.note: missing means the letter for note is taken out of the singing word

parts.note: to chant is to sing

explanation.surface: A bird starts to sing but leaves out a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops N from CHANT.
explanation.definitionFit: The chats are small songbirds such as the stonechat and whinchat.

clue.text: See ad and buy product, finally to be cooked now?

definitions.text: See ad and buy product, finally to be cooked now?

indicators.note: cooked means the preceding letters are mixed up as in a recipe
finally means only the last letter of product is used

explanation.surface: A shopper sees an advert, buys the food, and wonders whether it must be cooked straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: SEEAD, BUY and T (the last letter of 'product') are rearranged by 'to be cooked'; the whole clue also describes the date stamped on food.
explanation.definitionFit: The date printed on perishable food is the deadline by which it should be eaten or cooked.

clue.text: Explorer beginning to suffer with cold, excessively

indicators.note: beginning to means only the opening letter of suffer is taken

parts.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold
OTT, over the top, means excessively

explanation.surface: A polar explorer starts to suffer from the extreme cold.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT is British slang for 'over the top', meaning excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Falcon Scott led the doomed British expedition to the South Pole in 1912.

clue.text: Question asked by someone comparing Christmas presents etc?

definitions.text: Question asked by someone comparing Christmas presents
definitions.meaning: after telling a friend what they got, someone asks what the friend received in return
a casual phrase for 'and other things of that kind'

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a colloquial tail to a list, like 'and so on', and also literally asks about another's gifts.

clue.text: Enjoying fine weather? Something our readers probably won't be doing!

definitions.text: Something our readers probably won't be doing!
definitions.meaning: The Sun is a tabloid newspaper; Guardian readers are unlikely to buy it

explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper, and 'our readers' are Guardian readers, who would rarely take it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting out in sunshine is basking; buying a newspaper regularly is also called taking it.

clue.text: Economist's suggestion for a cannibal's feast?

definitions.meaning: Milton ... was the American monetarist economist
a cannibal might serve a person cooked in a pan

explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link ('is'); split into two words the surname becomes a cannibal's dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton Friedman won the Nobel prize in economics in 1976 as leader of the Chicago school.

clue.text: Some holy stranger encountered in place on missionary journey

definitions.text: encountered in place on missionary journey

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A holy stranger is met by travellers on a mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes part of 'holy stranger'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lystra, a town in Asia Minor, was visited by St Paul on his missionary travels in Acts.

clue.text: Security person with hairy bits at the front of University Hospital

indicators.note: at the front of places the hair before the university and the hospital

parts.note: locks are tresses of hair
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, a university

explanation.surface: A guard at a university hospital has hair hanging over his face.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesperson who fits and opens locks works in the security business.

clue.text: Reliable but losing heart — is worker, in terms of self-image?

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letter of the word for reliable is removed

parts.note: solid means reliable
an ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A dependable employee loses his nerve and starts doubting how he sees himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' takes the middle L from SOLID, leaving SOID.
explanation.definitionFit: The French term means self-styled or so-called, describing what someone claims to be.

clue.text: Sidney had curled up nice and warm, maybe

indicators.note: curled up suggests Sidney's letters twisted into a new shape

explanation.surface: Sidney has snuggled up and is cosy and comfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curled up' rearranges SIDNEYHAD. 'Nice and warm' is an example: two words joined by 'and' to express one idea (nicely warm).
explanation.definitionFit: This figure of speech expresses a single idea through two words linked by 'and', as nice and warm does.

clue.text: Fine instrument dramatist uses

indicators.note: uses means the word dramatist contains and employs the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: A playwright makes use of a fine instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uses' takes the run inside 'dramatist'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amati family of Cremona made violins prized as some of the finest ever built.

clue.text: It's not just the workers they look after

definitions.text: It's not just the workers they look after

parts.words: It's not just the workers they look after
parts.note: beekeepers tend a hive's queen and drones as well as its worker bees

explanation.walkthrough: 'workers' suggests employees, but these are the workers of a beehive.
explanation.definitionFit: Beekeepers look after colonies containing a queen and drones as well as worker bees.

clue.text: Liberal request made by independent political theorist, once

parts.note: to ask is to request

explanation.surface: A Liberal's demand is answered by an independent political thinker of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Laski was a British Labour Party thinker and LSE professor who died in 1950.

clue.text: Guy of 7 in short-staffed group

indicators.note: short means the word for staffed is cut by its final letter

parts.note: a staffed post is manned
a ring is a group, as of spies or criminals

explanation.surface: A man from the expedition joins a team that is short of staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts MANNED to MANNE. 7 is SCOTT: Guy Mannering is a novel by Sir Walter Scott, not the explorer.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy Mannering is the title character of Walter Scott's 1815 novel.

clue.text: Make a killing, maybe, as murderer keeping quiet

indicators.note: keeping means the murderer holds the word for quiet within him

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A murderer makes a killing while keeping silent about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a killing' looks like murder but means profit.
explanation.definitionFit: To profit from an opportunity is to cash in, and making a killing is a big profit.

clue.text: Casual society set up in the country

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are raised from bottom to top

parts.note: airy means casual or offhand

explanation.surface: A relaxed social club is founded out in the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns AIRY + S into AIRYS read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a Middle Eastern nation with Damascus as its capital.

clue.text: High priest's casual greeting, unusual around church

parts.note: hi is an informal hello

indicators.note: around means the word for unusual is turned about

parts.note: rare means unusual

explanation.surface: A high priest offers an informal hello in an unusual church.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link ('has'). 'around' here means turned round, not placed around church; the church comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: A hierarch is a chief priest or senior religious leader.

clue.text: Therapy that could come from a herb

indicators.note: could come from means the letters of a herb can be rearranged to produce the answer

explanation.surface: Herbal medicine might be the source of a treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could come from' rearranges AHERB.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehabilitation therapy is treatment to restore health, often for addiction.

clue.text: Fruit not looking so good, a third wasted

indicators.note: a third wasted means two of the six letters, a third of them, are lost

parts.note: uglier means less good-looking

explanation.surface: A fruit past its best, with a third of it gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a third wasted' removes ER, two of the six letters of UGLIER.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a lumpy Jamaican citrus fruit crossing grapefruit and tangerine.

clue.text: Message from 7 undone by a plod, a graft with sun, gales, ice

indicators.note: undone means the following words are unravelled and their letters reworked

explanation.surface: A message from a polar explorer, beaten by slogging, hard work, sun, gales and ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is SCOTT; this is his diary entry on reaching the South Pole. 'undone' rearranges all the letters from 'a plod' to 'ice'; the commas and 'by' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Falcon Scott wrote these words in his journal on reaching the South Pole in 1912.

clue.text: Cooks of now and yesteryear?

parts.note: Captain James Cook the explorer, and Alastair Cook who captained England at cricket

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooks' suggests chefs, but means two famous men named Cook: the 18th-century navigator and Alastair Cook, England's cricket captain when this appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Both James Cook and Alastair Cook held the title of leader, one of a ship and one of a cricket team.

clue.text: Hollow bishop with a thing to be confessed?

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a sin is what a penitent confesses

explanation.surface: A bishop has something on his conscience to confess.
explanation.definitionFit: A basin is a bowl or a hollow in the ground, as in a river basin.
